candidates.exact_span: "Water Quality Standards for Salinity - Colorado River System" by the Colorado River Basin Salinity Control Forum. In addition, the permit may be reopened and modified during the life of the permit if relevant procedures implementing the Water Quality Standards are either revised or promulgated by the New Mexico Environment Department. Should the State adopt a State water quality standard, and/or develop or amend a TMDL, this permit may be reopened to establish effluent limitations for the parameter(s) to be consistent with that approved State standard and/or water quality management plan, in accordance with 40 CFR §122.44(d). Modification of the permit is subject to the provisions of 40 CFR §124.5.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage ties salinity standards and potential future state-standard/TMDL actions to reopening the permit to establish effluent limitations. Different readings of whether current permit limits are definitive for FY2025, which parameters already have enforceable numeric limits, or whether some limits remain to be established could change applicable-limit determinations (A) and how missing or non-numeric results are classified when no operative limit is clear (C).

candidates.exact_span: No variance requests have been received.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Variances can alter or substitute enforceable numeric limits. Interpreting this statement as confirming that no variance-modified limits apply versus leaving open whether other variance mechanisms or timing could still affect limits could change which numeric limit is treated as applicable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The permit is in the process of certification by the State agency following regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §124.53.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Certification status can bear on whether permit conditions are operative and enforceable during the evaluation period. A different interpretation of what 'in the process of certification' means for FY2025 enforceability could change whether numeric limits (A) and stated monitoring obligations (B) are treated as currently binding.

candidates.exact_span: EPA Application Form 2A was received on April 13, 2021.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The application receipt date may anchor permit term, renewal timing, or phase-in of requirements. Different interpretations of how that date maps to the FY2025 permit year or effective monitoring schedule could change which monitoring obligations are deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Water, 20.6.4 NMAC, effective September 12, 2018.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This identifies the state water quality standard rule used to develop the permit. candidates.exact_span: EPA approved TMDL for the San Juan River Watershed (Part One)-Navajo Nation Boundary at the HogBack to Navajo Dam, May 10, 2005.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cited TMDL may inform wasteload allocations or effluent limitations for discharges in that watershed. Different readings of the TMDL's geographic scope, covered parameters, and whether its requirements have been fully translated into permit limits could change which numeric limits apply.
